source: Battambang Provincial Department of Agriculture and the Cambodia Northwest Provinces Fruit Culture Development Committee (financial support from the SEILA Programme), Khmer translation of Photpeechon Whayooathdee, "ដំណាំខ្នុរ (Jackfruit)", "Translation Copy No. 4", January 1997 (500 copies printed). This is a Khmer translation of a Thai-language original: Whayooathdee, Photpeechon, "Jackfruit (2nd edition)", Nonthaburi Province, Thailand: Agriculture Lover's Printing House, 1988. Cover illustration source: Forestry/Fuelwood Research and Development Project, 1992, "Growing Multipurpose Trees on Small Farms", Winrock International, Bangkok. Other artwork by Sarath, Som, Center for Social Development, Phnom Penh, Dec. 1996.
text:
This chapter addresses jackfruit's place in plant classification and the confusion around Khmer common names for closely related species in the same genus. The text explains that several tree species produce fruit similar in general appearance to jackfruit, and that Khmer speakers historically applied overlapping common names to them, causing confusion between true jackfruit and its relatives. The chapter distinguishes at least the following species/types, citing their scientific (Latin binomial) names as given in the source:

- "ខ្នុរធំធាត់" (a large-fruited type) — associated in the source with the scientific name Artocarpus champeden, described as originating from certain regions and having leaves and fruit forms distinguishable from the other species discussed.
- "ខ្នុរណាំង" — associated with Artocarpus integra or Artocarpus integrifolia (the source gives both forms and treats them as referring to the same species; modern botanical usage places true jackfruit under Artocarpus heterophyllus Lam., a synonym relationship the source itself gestures toward without using the modern binomial explicitly on this page). The text also gives the name Artocarpus integra (Thunb.) Merr. and the English common name "Jack-fruit" explicitly for this type, describing it as the tree most properly called "ខ្នុរ" (khnor) in Khmer.
- "ខ្នុរអំពិល" / breadfruit-type relatives — associated with Artocarpus communis (also written Artocarpus incisa in the source), with Khmer names given as "ការ៉ុប" (kaarob) and its relatives, described as visually similar to jackfruit but botanically distinct — these are breadfruit-type trees rather than true jackfruit.

The chapter stresses that "ខ្នុរណាំង" and true "ខ្នុរ" (jackfruit) are frequently confused in everyday Khmer usage, and gives comparative notes to help distinguish them: differences in leaf shape/texture, differences in the surface texture and spine pattern of the fruit rind, and differences in flesh texture and flavor (true jackfruit generally has firmer, more distinctly separated flesh segments/"bulbs" per the source's description). The chapter closes by noting that despite the botanical differences, in casual rural speech people often still lump all of these into the single word "ខ្នុរ", which is why careful growers and traders benefit from learning to tell the types apart before buying planting material or grafting stock.

Translation confidence note: the Latin binomials above are transcribed as printed in the scanned source; spelling/spacing in the original scan (e.g. "Artocarpus champenden" vs "champeden") could not be fully disambiguated from the image quality, so readers relying on the exact orthography should verify against a primary botanical reference.
